name: Archers of Loaf
label: Alias
lede: Four friends from Asheville made a $5,000 debut, got a Beavis and Butt-Head cameo, and turned down a major-label offer because of who else was on the roster.

eras.title: A riddle for a name
eras.text: Eric Bachmann, Eric Johnson, Matt Gentling and Mark Price start a band in Chapel Hill in 1991. Their first record is a giveaway inside a magazine.

years.src: Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf · Clash: Icky Mettle
years.h: Four friends from Asheville start a band in Chapel Hill
years.p: Eric Bachmann, Eric Johnson, Matt Gentling and Mark Price all grew up in Asheville. Bachmann had majored in saxophone at Appalachian State before he dropped out.
years.xp:
Asked about the name, Bachmann told Clash: "It's a riddle. It means something in Russian, but we intentionally mistranslated it." That is the whole official explanation.

The band formed in early 1991, per Wikipedia, and spent the next year in Chapel Hill before anyone outside town heard a note.

years.src: Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf · CREEM
years.h: The first record comes free inside Stay Free! magazine
years.p: "Wrong" and "South Carolina" make up a 7-inch given away with issue 1.
years.xp:
"South Carolina" later ended up on the My So-Called Life soundtrack, according to Wikipedia.

Bachmann told CREEM that Alias pressed only 1,000 copies of the band's first single: "it's definitely not 'Bridge Over Troubled Water.'"

eras.title: Icky Mettle and a cartoon nod
eras.text: A single, a debut and an MTV cameo in one year. Thirty years on, the record is still showing up on critics' best-of lists.

years.src: Wikipedia: Web in Front
years.h: Alias releases "Web in Front" and college radio picks it up
years.p: The 7-inch comes out in February 1993. Neil Strauss of the New York Times called it Bachmann's "tongue-in-cheek version of a love song."
years.xp: Alkaline Trio covered it in 2010, and Chris Carrabba of Dashboard Confessional recorded his own version in 2011. Pitchfork later ranked it number 77 on its list of the best tracks of the 1990s.

years.src: Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf · Wikipedia: Web in Front
yt: Beavis and Butt-Head do "Web in Front"
years.h: MTV's Beavis and Butt-Head sit through the "Web in Front" video
years.p: The clip airs in season 5. The song later lands on the Mallrats soundtrack in 1995, and an Archers poster is on the club door in Hackers.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the Beavis and Butt-Head episode as season 5. That is the closest date a source gives.

years.cap: Archers of Loaf at the Black Cat, Washington DC, January 8, 1994
years.src: Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Icky Mettle · CREEM
years.h: Dishes at 7 AM, Icky Mettle sessions from 2
years.p: Bachmann works at two restaurants while the band records after hours. Bandcamp Daily says the record cost a few thousand dollars from Alias.
years.xp:
Bandcamp Daily has Bachmann working mornings at the Carolina Coffee Shop and evenings at the New Orleans Cookery, sharing a bedroom with seven roommates, and tracking with producer Caleb Southern from about 2 AM to 6 AM at the Cat's Cradle once the floors were mopped. Bachmann puts it this way: "I'd record from two to about six."

Wikipedia gives a different picture: seven days at Kraptone Studios in Chapel Hill, and Bachmann saying "We spent like $5,000 to make it." Bachmann told CREEM he got through the restaurant shifts with cocaine: "I'd use it just to stay awake."

years.src: Wikipedia: Icky Mettle · Stereogum: Progress Report
yt: Full set, Trinity College, Hartford CT, July 28, 1993
years.h: Icky Mettle: 14 songs, 38 minutes
years.p: Robert Christgau gives the debut an A. Pitchfork later ranks it number 32 among the best albums of the 1990s.
years.xp:
Bandcamp Daily dates the record to 1994, but Wikipedia and the reissue campaign both say 1993.

Merge issued a deluxe edition in 2011, and Bachmann told Stereogum that Alias had lost the original artwork, so the covers were rebuilt from scratch.

eras.title: Chicago, Weezer and a stack of offers
eras.text: The follow-up gets cut in Chicago and the offers start arriving. The band spends 1995 saying no, and opening for Weezer.

years.cap: Archers of Loaf at the Middle East Downstairs, Cambridge, Massachusetts, around 1994
years.src: Wikipedia: Vee Vee · Bandcamp Daily
yt: Full set, Liquid Lounge, Norman OK, March 2, 1994
years.h: Stuck at the Canadian border, the band writes Vee Vee
years.p: They record the second album in Chicago in August 1994, with engineer Bob Weston.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits production to the band and [[Bob Weston|7364260a-0a3e-4a6c-bcf8-b4e743c0b2c0]]. Bandcamp Daily says the band wrote the songs while stuck trying to cross into Canada for scheduled gigs.

years.src: Wikipedia: Vee Vee
yt: Archers of Loaf interview and "Harnessed in Slums" video, MTV
years.h: "Harnessed in Slums" takes Vee Vee to college radio
years.p: Alias releases the second album on March 6, 1995, and Robert Christgau gives it another A. The single gets steady play on college and alternative stations.
years.xp: A two-disc Merge reissue with rarities, demos and B-sides followed on February 21, 2012.

years.big: "For us on Maverick, it'd be us and Candlebox and Alanis."
years.src: Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf
years.h: Maverick Records comes calling and gets a no
years.p: Drummer Mark Price on the Warner division's roster. Bachmann's objection was the Alias contract.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that Maverick, a Warner Music Group division, courted the band. Bachmann said the practical problem was the contract they had already signed with Alias: "If we would have had Maverick buy out our contract, we'd be however many thousands of dollars in debt to them."

years.src: Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf
yt: "Wrong" live at the Metro, Chicago, March 25, 1995
years.h: Weezer's crew is fine; the venue staff are the problem
years.p: On the 1995 tour opening for [[Weezer|6fe07aa5-fec0-4eca-a456-f29bff451b04]], Matt Gentling says the band had no beef with the Weezer guys. It was how the people working the venues treated opening acts.
years.xp: Gentling: "It wasn't as much that we didn't like the Weezer guys, but the opening bands get treated like crap by the people who work (at the venues)."

eras.title: Elektra, Seattle and the exit
eras.text: A major label handles distribution, the band makes its most polished record, and then the wheels come off. It ends in 1998 with a drummer's wrist.

years.src: Wikipedia: All the Nations Airports · Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf · Bandcamp Daily
yt: Live at the Mercury Theatre, Knoxville, 1996
years.h: Elektra distributes All the Nations Airports
years.p: Released September 24, 1996, and recorded at Ironwood Studios in Seattle with Brian Paulson. The band stays signed to Alias.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the sessions to March and April 1996. Gentling told an interviewer the band wanted to spend time on tone rather than repeating takes: "We took over a day (just) to get the drums sounding right."

Merge reissued it in 2012 in the US and Fire in the UK.

years.src: Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf
years.h: Home from the tour with no new songs, the band nearly quits
years.p: Bachmann says they got back from the All the Nations Airports tour with no idea what to write next.
years.xp:
Bachmann: "We got back and we were not real happy with the way that [the tour] went." The band decided to try once more, with a deadline: make another record, do another tour, "and if there's not another spark, we'll split up after that."

Wikipedia lists the Vitus Tinnitus EP on Alias in 1997.

years.src: Wikipedia: White Trash Heroes · Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf · Bandcamp Daily
years.h: White Trash Heroes gets built one part at a time
years.p: The fourth album drops the four-people-in-a-room sound for songs assembled layer by layer.
years.xp:
On "Banaging on a Dead Drum," the band swapped instruments: Johnson on drums, Gentling on slide guitar, Price on bass and Bachmann, the only one who knew it, on guitar.

Bachmann later told Bandcamp Daily there are "four or five great songs" and that on the rest "you can tell these guys are just really trying to finish a contract." Wikipedia notes the record was reissued by Merge in 2012 with new artwork by Casey Burns.

years.src: Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf
years.h: Brian Causey of Man or Astro-man? fills in for Johnson
years.p: Eric Johnson misses tour dates because of his day job. Causey plays guitar in his place.

years.big: "We were still friendly when we broke up."
years.src: Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf · Clash: Icky Mettle · Bandcamp Daily · Stereogum: Progress Report
years.h: Mark Price's carpal tunnel surgery ends the band
years.p: Eric Bachmann on the split. The last show is at the Cat's Cradle in Carrboro, and the tape is kept.
years.xp:
Clash describes a band worn out by touring, and Bandcamp Daily adds mismanagement to the list. Bachmann told Stereogum the split was not bitter.

The final Cat's Cradle show became the band's first official live album two years later.

eras.title: Thirteen years of side projects
eras.text: Everyone scatters and nobody calls it a hiatus. Bachmann's Crooked Fingers becomes his main outlet until a month in Taiwan changes his mind.

years.src: Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf
years.h: After the split, Bachmann starts Crooked Fingers and Johnson heads to law school
years.p: Bachmann records under his own name, as Barry Black and as [[Crooked Fingers|d935bec6-cab7-46cc-bf8b-ca089563b985]]. Johnson, as Spookie, releases an EP and an album and attends law school in North Carolina.
years.xp: Gentling plays bass with Crooked Fingers, tours with [[Superchunk|61653550-fd9b-4401-8248-44f2d064d384]], and has stints as a live bassist for [[Band of Horses|07b6020a-c539-4d68-aeef-f159f3befc76]], the Poles and Analog Moon, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf
years.h: Seconds Before the Accident keeps the last night on tape
years.p: Alias releases the band's first official live album, recorded at the final Cat's Cradle show.

years.big: "I realized I wanted to be playing music again."
years.src: Stereogum: Progress Report
years.h: A month teaching English in Taiwan ends nearly 13 years of silence
years.p: Eric Bachmann told Stereogum the trip is what made him call the other three.
years.xp: Bachmann said the band never broke up acrimoniously, and he was already worrying about age: "I'm 41. I can't be 65 years old and singing."

eras.title: The Loaf comes back
eras.text: An unannounced club show at home turns into festival dates, a late-night TV spot, four reissues and a concert film.

years.cap: Archers of Loaf at the Troubadour, West Hollywood, June 4, 2011
years.src: The A.V. Club · NPR Music: Sasquatch 2011 · Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf
years.h: The band turns up unannounced at the Cat's Cradle
years.p: They open for local act [[The Love Language|4ad96392-aa29-42b9-b319-9c9ea454a5b3]] on January 15, 2011. The A.V. Club reports it on January 17.
years.xp: They followed with Sasquatch! near Seattle on May 29, which NPR Music and KEXP recorded and broadcast.

years.cap: Archers of Loaf at the Middle East, Cambridge, Massachusetts, April 27, 2012
years.src: Pitchfork: Archers of Loaf Announce Reissue Campaign · Stereogum: Progress Report
years.h: Merge lines up four reissues, minus the artwork
years.p: Merge Records announces deluxe reissues of all four Alias albums, starting with Icky Mettle.
years.xp: Bachmann told Stereogum that Alias had "lost all the art work, all the files," so the artwork for every reissue had to be recreated.

years.cap: Archers of Loaf at the Troubadour, West Hollywood, June 4, 2011
years.src: Punknews: Archers of Loaf Wrong live on Fallon
years.h: "Wrong" goes out on NBC's Late Night with Jimmy Fallon
years.p: The band plays its 1993 song and Punknews posts the clip.

years.src: Seattle Times: What Did You Expect? · Wikipedia: Archers of Loaf
yt: "Web in Front" live at Cat's Cradle, August 20, 2011
years.h: What Did You Expect? puts the Cat's Cradle shows on film
years.p: Gorman Bechard's concert documentary, out in 2012, follows the band's August 2011 shows.
years.xp: The concert audio came out in 2015 as the double album Curse of the Loaf, produced by Brian Paulson, with the film and a poster in the deluxe package.

eras.title: A new record, 24 years on
eras.text: A YouTube teaser in 2019 leads to a first new song in more than 20 years, then an album on Merge.

years.src: Stereogum: Archers of Loaf Tease · Brooklyn Vegan: Raleigh Days
years.h: "Raleigh Days" is the first new Archers song since 1998
years.p: Stereogum reports a November 2019 teaser called "The Return of the Loaf." The song is released digitally on Merge on February 20.

years.src: CREEM · Bandcamp Daily · Consequence: Archers of Loaf Announce · Merge Records: Screaming Undercover
years.h: Reason in Decline ends a 24-year wait
years.p: Merge releases the fifth album after the singles "In the Surface Noise" and "Screaming Undercover," the latter with an animated video by Paul Friedrich.
years.xp:
Bachmann told CREEM that fits of debilitating depression slowed the writing. He also told Bandcamp Daily: "I don't know how to write from the 23-year-old me, and that's what people want."

Consequence reported the announcement on July 13, 2022, along with East Coast tour dates for late November and early December.
